@copilot Simplify this PR directly, without creating another PR as a workaround. The user requested the following reduction after reviewing the current implementation: check async appender configuration only when the SDK is installed via OpenTelemetryAppender.setOpenTelemetry(), not at three lifecycle points.

In instrumentation/logback/logback-appender-1.0/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/logback/appender/v1_0/OpenTelemetryAppender.java, retain the configuration check in setOpenTelemetry(), remove it from start() and append(), and remove asyncAppenderCheckedOnAppend and its restart/reset bookkeeping. Keep the once-per-appender warning flag, nested attachment detection, identity-based cycle protection, and class-name-based AsyncAppenderBase detection for compatibility with supported Logback releases that predate that class. Keep this an advisory Logback status warning, with appender names and recommended direct OTel attachment plus SDK batch export. Do not introduce async propagation or alter export behavior.

The accepted tradeoff is that configuration must be assembled before SDK installation. Appender graphs attached or changed afterward are not guaranteed to be detected until SDK installation is performed again. Update the relevant README explanation to state the installation-time check and this limitation without adding a dynamic reconfiguration mechanism.

Reduce the tests accordingly. Remove coverage solely for the deleted start/first-append detection hooks. Consolidate Spring Boot coverage around the actual SDK-installation path: OpenTelemetryAppenderAutoConfiguration.LogbackAppenderConfiguration calls OpenTelemetryAppender.install(openTelemetry); confirm the exact code and exercise the relevant existing integration path rather than relying on early LogbackAppenderInstaller.start() behavior. Retain focused coverage for once-only warnings across repeated installation, nested async paths, and directly attached OTel with separate async output preserving correlation and producing no warning. Keep the implementation and tests as small as the requirements allow; do not replace removed test boilerplate with unnecessary abstractions.

Run the narrowest relevant formatting tasks before targeted tests and report their actual results in your completion evidence. Keep changes limited to this simplification and its directly related documentation and tests. Preserve the existing draft state.

replies.body: Simplified as requested in `5ed9afc9`: async graph inspection now runs only during SDK installation, with lifecycle-hook coverage removed and Spring coverage routed through the `ApplicationReadyEvent` installer. The README documents the installation-time detection limitation. Focused formatting and tests passed.

+#### Asynchronous logging and trace correlation
+
+Attach `OpenTelemetryAppender` directly to your logger. Placing it behind Logback's `AsyncAppender`
+loses trace/span correlation because the logging thread's OpenTelemetry context is not propagated
+to the async worker. This limitation does not apply to the Java agent's automatic log capture.
+
+Use the SDK's `BatchLogRecordProcessor` for asynchronous export. Formatting and attribute extraction
+still run on the logging thread. Console or file appenders can remain asynchronous, as shown below:
+
+```xml
+<configuration>
+  <appender name="console" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
+    <encoder>
+      <pattern>%d{HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
+    </encoder>
+  </appender>
+  <appender name="async-console" class="ch.qos.logback.classic.AsyncAppender">
+    <appender-ref ref="console"/>
+  </appender>
+  <appender name="OpenTelemetry"
+            class="io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.logback.appender.v1_0.OpenTelemetryAppender"/>
+  <root level="INFO">
+    <appender-ref ref="OpenTelemetry"/>
+    <appender-ref ref="async-console"/>
+  </root>
+</configuration>
+```
+
+With the OpenTelemetry Spring Boot starter, use the same layout in `logback-spring.xml`. The starter
+configures SDK batch export by default.
+
+When the SDK is installed, `OpenTelemetryAppender` checks the configuration and warns once if it is
+behind a Logback async appender. Configure appenders before installing the SDK; later changes are
+not checked automatically. The warning does not change logging behavior.

Keep meaningful coverage, but reduce unnecessary setup and repeated assertions in instrumentation/logback/logback-appender-1.0/library/src/asyncAppenderTest/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/logback/appender/v1_0/AsyncAppenderWarningTest.java.

The existing AsyncOpenTelemetryAppenderTest already covers the basic warning through OpenTelemetryAppender.install(). Trim the XML configuration case in AsyncAppenderWarningTest to focus on warning timing and deduplication through setOpenTelemetry(): no warning before SDK installation, one warning when installed, and still one warning after repeated installation. Avoid repeating basic log-export assertions already covered elsewhere.

Keep one focused nested traversal case proving the warning finds the async boundary through synchronous wrappers and nested async appenders. Keep the recommended-setup case proving directly attached OTel with separate async output emits no warning and preserves span correlation. Simplify the custom forwarding-appender fixture where practical, without introducing unnecessary helpers or abstractions. Preserve meaningful existing assertions and keep production behavior unchanged.

Keep this change limited to test simplification. Do not change production code or remove the distinct timing, deduplication, nested traversal, or recommended-setup coverage. Run the narrowest applicable formatting task before targeted async-appender tests and report the actual results in your completion evidence. Preserve the PR's existing draft/ready state. Update this PR rather than creating another PR as a workaround.
